title: A2A Supply-chain Signal Payload v1
description:
Payload shape for the `supply-chain-signal` A2A message type (spec §16.6, v2.6 — E-SC-7). Carried as the `payload` of an `a2a-envelope-v1` whose `message_type` is `supply-chain-signal`.

Consent model: bidirectional opt-in. A Brain MUST declare `supply-chain-signal` in its Agent Card `capabilities.accepts[]` to receive signals; MUST declare it in `capabilities.emits[]` to send signals. A Brain MUST NOT send a `supply-chain-signal` to a peer whose Agent Card does not declare `supply-chain-signal` in `accepts[]`. This is a tighter posture than the one-direction-by-Agent-Card-declaration default for other A2A message types — see §16.6 rationale (legal exposure, false-positive multiplication).

Language discipline: published findings MUST use non-attributive language per §16.4. The `legal_disclaimer` field is a forcing function: implementations SHOULD populate it with a short, conservative-language summary that operators can quote in human-facing reports without legal review on each finding.

Receivers MUST treat signals as advisory input. Receivers MAY aggregate signals across peers via `cross_brain_count` to support 'two independent peers flagged this package' confidence signals; aggregation rules are implementation-defined in v1 and a candidate for normative specification in a future version.

schema_version.description: Payload schema version. Independent from the enclosing `a2a-envelope-v1` schema_version.

advisory_id.description: Optional canonical advisory identifier (CVE-YYYY-NNNNN, RUSTSEC-YYYY-NNNN, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, OSV-YYYY-NNNN, etc.). Absent for vigilance/agent-review signals that did not produce a registry-tracked advisory.

name.description: Package name as it appears in its registry.

version.description: The specific version that triggered the signal (e.g., '1.82.7'). For range-based advisories, this SHOULD be the highest version observed in the originating Brain's dependency graph.

version_range.description: Optional. The full affected version range as documented by the originating advisory (e.g., '>=1.82.7,<1.82.9').

severity_class.description: Severity classification. `informational` covers RustSec-style 'unmaintained' notices and other no-active-vulnerability-but-worth-knowing signals. Implementations SHOULD use the source advisory's severity when present and SHOULD default to `informational` for vigilance/agent-review signals without a registry severity.

discovery_source.description: Where the signal originated. `osv`/`rustsec`/`pypa`/`ghsa` indicate Layer 1 mechanical SCA matches. `vigilance` indicates a Layer 2 deep-signal heuristic. `agent-review` indicates a Layer 3 agent finding. `operator` indicates a manual operator-authored signal. `other` for sources not enumerated.

peer_brain_id.description: Identifier of the originating Brain. Matches the id in its Agent Card.

cross_brain_count.description: How many peer Brains (including the originator) have independently surfaced this signal. Supports 'two independent peers flagged this package' confidence signals. Defaults to 1 (originator only). Aggregation rules are implementation-defined in v1.

discovered_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the originating Brain first detected the signal. Receivers MAY use this for staleness checks.

advisory_uri.description: Optional pointer to the canonical advisory page (OSV.dev advisory URL, RustSec advisory file, GHSA URL, etc.).

summary.description: Short prose summary of the signal (one sentence). Non-attributive language REQUIRED per §16.4 — describe behavior or pattern, not maintainer intent.

legal_disclaimer.description: Conservative-language summary suitable for inclusion in human-facing reports without per-finding legal review. Forcing function for §16.4's non-attributive-language requirement. Implementations SHOULD populate this for any signal shared with peers; receivers SHOULD prefer this field over `summary` when displaying findings to humans.

recommended_action.description: Optional originator-recommended action. Receivers MUST treat as advisory; the human-decision gate per §16.4 still applies on the receiver side.

metadata.description: Optional implementation-defined metadata (e.g., originating CMDB path, scenario id, evidence URIs). Implementations SHOULD avoid placing PII or secrets here.
